entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0436: Vulnerability in calamine
entry.summary: Panic and unbounded allocation (OOM) in the CFB/OLE2 parser on malformed input
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0436

Panic and unbounded allocation (OOM) in the CFB/OLE2 parser on malformed input
Reported
October 28, 2026
Issued
November 3, 2026
Package
calamine (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • denial-of-service
Keywords
#dos #panic #oom #cfb #ole2 #xls #xlsb
References
  • https://github.com/tafia/calamine/pull/762
CVSS Score
7.5 HIGH
CVSS Details
Attack Vector
Network
Attack Complexity
Low
Privileges Required
None
User Interaction
None
Scope
Unchanged
Confidentiality Impact
None
Integrity Impact
None
Availability Impact
High
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
Patched
  • >=0.38.0

Description

The Compound File Binary (OLE2) parser (src/cfb.rs), used when reading .xls and .xlsb workbooks and when extracting VBA projects from .xlsx, can panic or allocate without bound on crafted input. Both are reachable through the public reader API (open_workbook, Xls::new, Xlsb::new) on an attacker-supplied file. Impact is denial of service only — no memory unsafety (safe Rust turns the out-of-bounds read into a bounds-checked panic).

  1. Reachable panic (out-of-bounds slice index). The directory stream is iterated with .chunks(128), but Directory::from_slice reads fixed offsets (buf[..64], buf[116..120], buf[120..128]) without checking the chunk length. A directory stream whose length is not a multiple of 128 yields a short final chunk, causing a panic (range end index 64 out of range for slice of length N). SectorSize::Small 64-byte mini sectors are a second trigger.

  2. Unbounded allocation / OOM. The DIFAT loader grows the difat vector without bounding the number of iterations; a crafted self-referential DIFAT chain drives a multi-gigabyte allocation from a tiny file (a 512-byte file attempts an allocation of several gigabytes).

A consumer that parses untrusted or user-supplied spreadsheets can be crashed (thread panic, or process abort under panic=abort) or driven out of memory by a small crafted file.

Fixed in calamine 0.38.0 (commit b8ec4f0); the maintainer confirmed the fix in https://github.com/tafia/calamine/pull/762.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:H/A:N
Patched
no patched versions
Affected Functions
Version
ant_releases::AntReleaseRepoActions::extract_release_archive
  • <=0.4.3

Description

ant-releases downloads and unpacks release archives from the safe_network / autonomi repositories. When it extracts an archive, it builds each output path by joining the archive entry's own name onto the destination directory, with no check for .. or absolute components — a classic "zip-slip" path traversal (CWE-22 / CWE-23). A crafted archive can therefore create or overwrite files outside the intended extraction directory.

In extract_release_archive (src/lib.rs), the ZIP branch does:

let out_path = dest_dir_path.join(file.name());   // raw zip entry name, no containment check
if file.name().ends_with('/') {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&out_path)?;          // dir created outside dest_dir
} else {
    let mut outfile = std::fs::File::create(&out_path)?;   // file written outside dest_dir
    std::io::copy(&mut file, &mut outfile)?;
}

Proof of concept

A one-entry ZIP whose entry name is ../foo_pwned.txt, passed to AntReleaseRepoActions::extract_release_archive (obtained via the crate's public <dyn AntReleaseRepoActions>::default_config()), writes foo_pwned.txt as a sibling of the destination directory, outside it. Confirmed against the published 0.4.3 crate.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0430: Vulnerability in rio-vt
entry.summary: Path traversal in `rio-vt` Kitty graphics protocol handler allows out-of-bounds file delete (and read)
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0430

Path traversal in rio-vt Kitty graphics protocol handler allows out-of-bounds file delete (and read)
Reported
November 1, 2026
Issued

rio-vt (crates.io)

#path-traversal #kitty-graphics-protocol #file-disclosure #terminal
References

  • https://github.com/raphamorim/rio/pull/1998
CVSS Score

Required

Integrity Impact

Availability Impact
None
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N
Patched
  • >=0.5.29
Affected Functions
Version
rio_vt::ansi::kitty_graphics_protocol::parse
  • <=0.5.28

Description

The Kitty graphics protocol handler in rio-vt builds a filesystem path from an attacker-controlled APC escape sequence and, for the temp-file medium, only checks that the path contains the substring "tty-graphics-protocol" before it opens, reads, and remove_files it. There is no .. rejection and no canonicalization, so a path containing the marker substring plus .. escapes the terminal's temp directory (path traversal, CWE-22/CWE-23).

Because a terminal renders whatever arrives on the PTY (ssh output, a cat'd file, CI logs), untrusted output can delete a file outside the temp area and cause its bytes to be read back in.

Details

The sink is create_graphic_data() in src/ansi/kitty_graphics_protocol.rs, in the TransmissionMedium::TempFile branch, reachable through the public API rio_vt::ansi::kitty_graphics_protocol::parse. The path is the base64 APC payload of an a=t,t=t command, and the guard is:

let path = Path::new(path_str);
if !path.is_file() { return Err(GraphicError::FileNotFound); }       // literal path, resolves `..`
// reject /proc/ /sys/ /dev/ (lowercased substring)
if cmd.medium == TransmissionMedium::TempFile
    && !path_str.contains("tty-graphics-protocol") {                 // SUBSTRING, not a component
    return Err(GraphicError::InvalidData);
}
// ...
let mut file = File::open(path)...;          // reads file bytes
if cmd.medium == TransmissionMedium::TempFile {
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(path);      // deletes the file
}

This affects any terminal emulator or application built on rio-vt (e.g. the Rio terminal) that renders attacker-influenced output: an out-of-bounds file is deleted, and its contents are read into the process.

The fix

Fixed in rio-vt 0.5.29 (Rio 0.5.29) by PR #1998. For the temp-file medium the parent directory is resolved with canonicalize before any check, the resolved entry must lie inside a temp directory (temp_dir(), /tmp or /dev/shm) and contain the marker, and the delete goes through unlinkat on a handle to the validated directory, so neither .. nor a swapped symlink can redirect it. Path checks for the file medium also run on the file actually opened.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0435: Vulnerability in thrift
entry.summary: Unbounded memory allocation in `thrift` binary protocol `read_bytes`
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0435

Unbounded memory allocation in thrift binary protocol read_bytes
Reported

CVSS Score
7.5 HIGH
CVSS Details
Attack Vector
Network
Attack Complexity
Low
Privileges Required
None

None
Scope
Unchanged
Confidentiality Impact
None
Integrity Impact
None
Availability Impact
High
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
Patched
  • >=0.23.0
Affected Functions
Version
thrift::protocol::binary::TBinaryInputProtocol::read_bytes
  • <0.23.0
thrift::protocol::binary::TBinaryInputProtocol::read_string
  • <0.23.0

Description

Affected versions of the thrift crate size a buffer directly from an attacker-controlled 4-byte length read off the wire, before reading any payload and with no upper bound, allowing a hostile peer to force a large eager allocation or an immediate abort (denial of service, CWE-400 / CWE-789). This is the Rust implementation's instance of the CVE-2020-13949 pattern, published by the Apache Thrift PMC as CVE-2026-43868.

Details

In TBinaryInputProtocol::read_bytes (src/protocol/binary.rs), the length is read as a i32 from the transport and cast straight to usize to size a zeroing buffer before any payload is read:

fn read_bytes(&mut self) -> crate::Result<Vec<u8>> {
    let num_bytes = self.transport.read_i32::<BigEndian>()? as usize; // length from the wire
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; num_bytes];                               // unbounded eager allocation
    self.transport.read_exact(&mut buf).map(|_| buf).map_err(From::from)
}

There is no check that num_bytes is non-negative or that it fits within the data actually available:

  • A length of 0x7FFFFFFF forces a ~2 GiB allocation; 0x20000000 forces 512 MiB; and so on, from only a 4-byte input.
  • A negative length casts to a huge usize (up to usize::MAX), causing an immediate allocation failure / abort.

read_string routes through read_bytes, so string fields are affected the same way. The sink is reachable from any peer sending binary-protocol data, so this is an unauthenticated, network-reachable denial of service.

The fix

From thrift 0.23.0 onward, read_bytes goes through read_binary_len, which rejects negative sizes and enforces TConfiguration::max_string_size (default 100 MiB), alongside default message, frame, and recursion limits.

A separate, related gap on the non-strict message-name path was published as CVE-2026-58389 and fixed in 0.24.0; this advisory covers the read_bytes unbounded allocation (CVE-2026-43868), fixed in 0.23.0.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0433: Vulnerability in pulldown-cmark
entry.summary: Quadratic parsing of nested image wikilinks with `ENABLE_WIKILINKS`

Quadratic parsing of nested image wikilinks with ENABLE_WIKILINKS

CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
Patched
  • >=0.13.6
Unaffected
  • <0.13.0

Description

With Options::ENABLE_WIKILINKS, handle_wikilink builds a wikilink's target from the raw text of its body: scan_wikilink_pipe walks it looking for |, then contains('\0') and from_replace_nuls walk it again. Once a wikilink is created, disable_all_links only disables Link entries, so every enclosing ![[ stays live on the wikilink stack. On ![[![[![[…]]]]]] each of those openers then resolves in turn and rescans everything inside it, which is quadratic in the nesting depth. The event count stays tiny, because in the unpiped case each enclosing image replaces its body with a fresh text node, so all of that work is thrown away.

Applications that parse untrusted Markdown with ENABLE_WIKILINKS set, including through Options::all(), are affected. The option is off by default. Parsing without it is not affected.

The flaw was fixed in #1186 and released in 0.13.6.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

Patched

Unaffected
  • <0.11.0
Affected Functions
Version
evtx::wevt_templates::wevtcache::WevtCacheReader::next_entry
  • >=0.11.0, <0.15.1
evtx::wevt_templates::wevtcache::for_each_crim_blob
  • >=0.11.0, <0.15.1

Description

Affected versions of evtx did not bound a per-entry payload length read from a .wevtcache file before allocating a buffer sized from it, allowing a tiny crafted file to force a multi-gigabyte allocation and abort the process (out-of-memory denial of service, CWE-400).

Details

In WevtCacheReader::next_entry (src/wevt_templates/wevtcache.rs), the per-entry payload length is read as a u64 straight from the file and used to size a zeroing buffer before any data is read:

let len = usize::try_from(len_u64)?;   // u64 taken directly from the entry header
let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];          // unbounded allocation, sized from the file
reader.read_exact(&mut buf)?;          // only fails AFTER the allocation

The only check on len is that it fits in usize; there is no check that it fits within the bytes remaining in the file. An entry header declaring a ~4 GiB length therefore makes the crate request a ~4 GiB allocation from a file of only ~25 bytes.

The sink is reachable through the public API evtx::wevt_templates::wevtcache::for_each_crim_blob(path, f) (and the WevtCacheReader::next_entry it drives). The .wevtcache reader first shipped in 0.11.0, and every published version from 0.11.0 through 0.14.0 is affected. The code lives in the wevt_templates feature, which is enabled by default through the evtx_dump feature. The fix landed in 0.15.1: 0.15.0 was tagged but never published to crates.io (its Windows build failed), so 0.15.1 is the first patched release available. The Python bindings (evtx on PyPI) carry the fix as of 0.15.0.

Reproduction

A ~25-byte file is sufficient: the .wevtcache magic (WEVTCACH), a version (u32 LE) of 1, an entry_count (u32 LE) of 1, then one entry consisting of a kind byte and a len (u64 LE) set to a large value (e.g. 0xFFFFFFF0), with no payload bytes following. Passing that file to for_each_crim_blob triggers the oversized allocation before the short read fails.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0432: Vulnerability in codeq
entry.summary: `codeq`: decoding untrusted input can allocate memory from an unchecked length prefix (denial of service)
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0432

codeq: decoding untrusted input can allocate memory from an unchecked length prefix (denial of service)
Reported
October 31, 2026
Issued
November 2, 2026
Package
codeq (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • denial-of-service
Keywords
#denial-of-service #allocation #untrusted-input #oom
References
  • https://github.com/drmingdrmer/codeq/issues/4
CVSS Score
5.3 MEDIUM
CVSS Details
Attack Vector
Network
Attack Complexity
Low
Privileges Required
None
User Interaction
None
Scope
Unchanged
Confidentiality Impact
None
Integrity Impact
None
Availability Impact
Low
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L
Patched
  • >=0.6.3

Description

codeq is a serialization library whose Decode trait reads length-prefixed values. For String and Vec<u8>, the length-prefixed Decode implementations read a 4-byte big-endian length and allocate a buffer of that size before reading the payload. Because the declared length is taken straight from the input with no upper bound and no cross-check against the bytes actually available, a tiny input can force an allocation of up to ~4 GiB. Code that decodes untrusted data through codeq can therefore be made to spike memory use and be OOM-killed (CWE-400, uncontrolled resource consumption).

The affected path, in src/codec/impls/string_impl.rs:

impl Decode for String {
    fn decode<R: io::Read>(mut r: R) -> Result<Self, io::Error> {
        let len = r.read_u32::<BigEndian>()? as usize;
        let mut buf = vec![0; len];   // allocates `len` bytes up front
        r.read_exact(&mut buf)?; 
        String::from_utf8(buf).map_err(|e| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, e))
    }
}

Any code that decodes attacker-controlled bytes through codeq can be forcedcto allocate up to ~4 GiB per decode call from a 4-byte length prefix. On a service decoding untrusted input this is a cheap denial of service (crash / OOM-kill). The practical severity depends on how the embedding wires codeq to untrusted bytes.

Remediation

Fixed in 0.6.3, which grows the decode buffers as payload bytes actually arrive instead of pre-allocating the full declared length (commit 9f15313, "fix: codec: grow decode buffers as payload bytes arrive"). Upgrade to codeq >= 0.6.3.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0429: Vulnerability in zip
entry.summary: zip: `ZipArchive::extract` aborts the process on a symlink entry with a large declared size
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0429

zip: ZipArchive::extract aborts the process on a symlink entry with a large declared size
Reported
October 22, 2026
Issued
November 2, 2026
Package
zip (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • denial-of-service
Keywords
#dos #symlink #unbounded-allocation #extract
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-115909
  • GHSA-q7v9-x93c-xqv3
CVSS Score
7.5 HIGH
CVSS Details
Attack Vector
Network
Attack Complexity
Low
Privileges Required
None
User Interaction
None
Scope
Unchanged
Confidentiality Impact
None
Integrity Impact
None
Availability Impact
High
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
Patched
  • >=9.0.0

Description

ZipArchive::extract() sizes the symlink-target buffer from the uncompressed size declared in the central directory record, before reading a single byte of entry data:

let mut target = Vec::with_capacity(file.size() as usize);

Both inputs are attacker-controlled. ZipFile::size() returns uncompressed_size verbatim from the central directory, widened to a full u64 by a ZIP64 extended-information extra field, and is never cross-checked against the compressed size, the remaining archive length, or any platform-appropriate bound for a symlink target. ZipFile::is_symlink() is decided entirely by the S_IFLNK bit of the external-attributes field.

Vec::with_capacity() is infallible: when the reservation is refused it calls handle_alloc_error() and aborts the process. This is not a Rust panic. It is not caught by catch_unwind(), is unaffected by panic = "unwind", and is not contained by running the call on a worker thread.

A 112-byte archive is sufficient. One Stored entry flagged S_IFLNK with a ZIP64 field declaring uncompressed_size = 2^62 and a zero-byte payload makes extract() fail with:

memory allocation of 4611686018427387904 bytes failed
Aborted (core dumped)          # exit 134

The declared value only needs to exceed the host's address space, not its RAM: Vec::with_capacity() maps address space without touching pages, so resident memory stays flat and the abort happens on the refused reservation itself. Under a ulimit -v cap or a memory-constrained container the threshold drops far enough that a plain 32-bit uncompressed_size with no ZIP64 field suffices.

Applications that extract archives from untrusted input are affected on Unix and Windows targets with default features and no special configuration: upload handling, mail-attachment processing, package and artefact ingestion, backup restore and container-image layer extraction. No confidentiality or integrity property is affected: there is no memory unsafety, no out-of-bounds access, no disclosure and no data corruption.

The fix landed in zip-rs/zip2#984 and shipped in 9.0.0.

For further details see: https://github.com/zip-rs/zip2/security/advisories/GHSA-q7v9-x93c-xqv3

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0428: Vulnerability in orion
entry.summary: BLAKE2b produces wrong tag when using `reset()` with a different-length key
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0428

BLAKE2b produces wrong tag when using reset() with a different-length key
Reported
October 30, 2026
Issued
October 30, 2026
Package
orion (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • crypto-failure
Aliases
  • GHSA-xcc6-f2jq-43x6
References
  • https://github.com/orion-rs/orion/pull/690
Patched
  • ^0.17.16
  • >=0.18.1
Affected Functions
Version
orion::hazardous::mac::blake2b::Blake2b::reset
  • <0.17.16
  • <0.18.1
  • >=0.12.0

Description

Summary

hazardous::mac::blake2b::Blake2b::reset() does not correctly reset the state when a key is supplied that has a different length than the one used upon initialization with hazardous::mac::blake2b::Blake2b::new(), because it errorneously uses a cached length.

Impact

Initialization hazardous::mac::blake2b::Blake2b with a key of some length N, followed by a reset with a key of length != N will produce an incorrect BLAKE2b tag, causing hazardous::mac::blake2b::Blake2b::verify() to fail. This means under honest protocol conditions, parties could experience failing tag verifications.

Resolution

Upgrade to v0.17.16 or v0.18.1.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0426: Vulnerability in orion
entry.summary: LLVM introduces timing-vulnerable optimizations into ML-KEM and ML-DSA operations intended to be constant-time
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0426

LLVM introduces timing-vulnerable optimizations into ML-KEM and ML-DSA operations intended to be constant-time
Reported
October 30, 2026
Issued
October 30, 2026
Package
orion (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • crypto-failure
Aliases
  • GHSA-r7wm-4vf2-h44w
References
  • https://github.com/orion-rs/orion/pull/689
Patched
  • ^0.17.16
  • >=0.18.1
Affected Architectures
  • s390x
  • x86
  • x86_64

Description

Summary

On targets that do not have a conditional move/select operations, LLVM compiles the internal conditional_sub_u32() function, into one that will contain a conditional jump on secret-dependent data, which could leak information about encapsulation and signing keys.

conditional_sub_u32() is used throughout the field arithmetic of both ML-KEM and ML-DSA.

Impact

The variable-time jumps have been observed for ML-KEM and ML-DSA on:

  • i586-unknown-linux-gnu
  • s390x-unknown-linux-gnu

Additionally, ML-DSA sees the vulnerable LLVM optimization on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, for hazardous::dsa::mldsa44 and hazardous::dsa::mldsa87.

The leakage this LLVM optimization introduces could enable recovery of cryptographic secrets. The practicality of exploiting the leakage depends on the compiler, target CPU used and how "close" to the process using the vulnerable functions the attacker is.

Resolution

Upgrade to v0.17.16 or v0.18.1. conditional_sub_u32() has been re-written to take conditional-move/jump ops availability into account.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

  • <0.6.0

Description

Decoder::unpack does not safely contain the paths it extracts, so a malicious NAR archive can create files outside the destination directory — a path traversal (CWE-22).

In src/dec.rs (Decoder::unpack):

  • A symlink entry's target is written without checking where it points (src/dec.rs:153), so the archive can create a symlink that escapes the destination directory.
  • The out-of-destination containment check compares path strings only and does not account for symlinks created earlier in the same unpack (src/dec.rs:176-181), before reaching the write sinks (std::fs::create_dir at src/dec.rs:201 and OpenOptions::open at src/dec.rs:218).
  • The parser also accepts entry names containing / (src/parser.rs:138-147).

Combined, a malicious archive can include a symlink a pointing at an external directory and then an entry named a/b, causing b to be written to <external>/b, outside the destination. This can create new files anywhere the process can write (it cannot overwrite existing files), which is escalatable to code execution by planting files in attacker-chosen locations.

  • <=0.3.1

Description

SafeReleaseRepoActions::extract_release_archive builds each output path from the raw archive entry name and writes to it with no traversal check, so a malicious release archive can create directories and write files outside the destination directory, a "zip-slip" / path traversal (CWE-22 / CWE-23).

In src/lib.rs (extract_release_archive, zip branch):

let mut file = archive.by_index(i)?;
let out_path = dest_dir_path.join(file.name());   // file.name() is the raw entry name
if file.name().ends_with('/') {
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&out_path)?;          // no `..` check
} else {
    let mut outfile = std::fs::File::create(&out_path)?;   // writes outside dest
    std::io::copy(&mut file, &mut outfile)?;
}

The crate is unmaintained (latest release 0.3.1, 2024-10-22) and no fixed version is available.

Description

The parser of juniper called itself once for each level of nesting in a GraphQL document. The parser had no limit on the nesting depth. Deeply nested selection sets, input values, and list types thus overflowed the stack of the thread that parsed the document. Validation and execution followed fragment spreads in the same recursive way. Long chains of fragment spreads thus overflowed the stack in validation and execution.

A stack overflow aborts the whole process. One request can thus stop a server and drop all other requests in progress. The request needs no authentication.

juniper 0.17.2 rejects documents that nest deeper than 64 levels or contain more than 15,000 tokens. RootNode::limit_depth() and RootNode::limit_tokens() change the limits.

Description

Several parts of juniper did work that grew faster than the size of the GraphQL document. A small document could thus use seconds of CPU time or gigabytes of memory. The requests need no authentication.

  • OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged compared all pairs of fields with the same response name. The rule also reported one error for each pair of conflicting fields.
  • NoFragmentCycles and OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged visited a fragment again for each path that spread the fragment. Validation time thus doubled with each fragment that spread the next fragment twice.
  • Execution resolved the fields of a fragment once for each spread of the fragment. A document of 1.2 KB could expand into a billion fields.
  • The parser removed each token from the front of a vector. Parsing time thus grew with the square of the number of tokens.

juniper 0.17.2 fixes the issues. The parser rejects documents with more than 15,000 tokens and operations with more than 15,000 fields after the expansion of fragments. The validation rules visit each fragment once. OverlappingFieldsCanBeMerged stops after 100,000 field comparisons and reports at most 100 conflicts. RootNode::limit_tokens() and RootNode::limit_fields() change the limits.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0418: Vulnerability in libz-sys
entry.summary: libz-sys build script leaks environment variables in the build directory
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0418

libz-sys build script leaks environment variables in the build directory
Reported
October 28, 2026
Issued
October 29, 2026
Package
libz-sys (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Keywords
#build-script #environment #secrets
Aliases
  • GHSA-8p3x-q3q3-q3v5
References
  • https://github.com/rust-lang/libz-sys/pull/280
Patched
  • >=1.1.31
Unaffected
  • <1.0.21

Description

The build script of libz-sys version <= 1.1.30 prints the full environment of the build, including any secrets it contains, to its stdout when compiled with cc@1.6.0 or later on a Unix host. This affects any build that depends on libz-sys. Cargo saves build script stdout under target/, so the values end up in anything that stores or shares the target/ directory, such as CI caches.

This is similar to the Miri issue.

Details

To decide whether to link against a system zlib, the libz-sys build script compiles a small test program with a compiler command from cc and logs it with:

println!("running {:?}", cmd);

On Unix, Debug impl for std::process::Command prints every environment variable explicitly set on the command. Before cc@1.6.0, its Tool::to_command() set only a few compiler-specific variables. Starting with cc@1.6.0 (released 2026-10-03), Tool::to_command() clears the environment and sets every variable explicitly.

Cargo parses build script stdout for cargo: directives, and stores the full output in the build directory. It also prints it with -vv.

The probe runs for a default libz-sys build, including when pkg-config finds zlib, unless one of these applies:

  • the target is Windows, Android, Haiku or OpenHarmony
  • static linking is requested via the static feature or LIBZ_SYS_STATIC=1
  • the zlib-ng features are enabled without stock-zlib

Mitigations

Fixed in libz-sys@1.1.31, which no longer logs the probe command.

If you cannot upgrade, here are some workarounds:

  • Build with LIBZ_SYS_STATIC=1 or the static feature, which skips the probe.
  • Pin cc to a release before 1.6.0 (cargo update cc --precise <version>).

Note that upgrading libz-sys does not remove values already written. If an affected build already ran with secrets in its environment, clear CI caches and stored artifacts containing its target/build directory, and consider rotating those secrets.
